ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: In the circuit shown in figure, the symmetrical load in a delta connection has a line voltage \( U = 220V \), a resistance of 30Ω, and an inductive reactance of 40Ω per phase. Find the phase current.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are three external lines labeled A, C, B, the internal three impedance elements are labeled ZA, ZB, ZC, and these three impedances are connected end to end to form a triangular load structure, indicating that the load is a triangular (delta) connection. Reasoning: The given line voltage U_line = 220 V, each phase resistance R = 30 Ω, each phase inductive reactance X_L = 40 Ω. The magnitude of each phase impedance is |Z| = sqrt(R^2 + X_L^2) = sqrt(30^2 + 40^2) = sqrt(2500) = 50 Ω. Since the figure is a delta connection, in a triangular connection the phase voltage is equal to the line voltage, so U_phase = U_line = 220 V. Therefore the phase current I_phase = U_phase / |Z| = 220 / 50 = 4.4 A.

method.method_draft: Identify the diagram as a balanced delta. From the text, form the delta phase impedance magnitude |Z_delta| = sqrt(30^2 + 40^2) = 50 ohm. Convert to an equivalent star impedance magnitude |Z_Y| = 50/3 ohm. The equivalent star phase voltage is 220/sqrt(3) V, so the line current is I_line = (220/sqrt(3))/(50/3) = sqrt(3)*220/50. Convert back to delta phase current using I_phase_delta = I_line/sqrt(3), giving 220/50 = 4.4 A.
